## 💡 About this resource

This practical guide helps you build discrete-event simulation models (DES) which are **reproducible** and part of a robust **reproducible analytical pipeline (RAP)** - a structured, automated, and repeatable approach to analysis. [Learn more →](pages/intro/rap.qmd)

**Packages we use:**

| Tool | Purpose | Link |
| - | - | - |
| 🐍 SimPy | DES in Python | <https://simpy.readthedocs.io/en/latest/> |
| 🧮 simmer | DES in R | <https://r-simmer.org/> |

<div class="h2-tight"></div>

## 🗺️ Why use this guide?

* **Build models that last.** Set up your projects in a way that's easy to run, revisit, and reuse - whether it's tomorrow or next year.

* **Informed by best practice.** It adheres to recommendations from [Heather et al. 2025](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2501.13137) and the ["Levels of RAP" framework](https://nhsdigital.github.io/rap-community-of-practice/introduction_to_RAP/levels_of_RAP/) from the NHS RAP Community of Practice. . [Learn more →](pages/intro/guidelines.qmd)

* **Not just for healthcare.** The coding and reproducibility tips are useful to all kinds of models, fields, and analysis techniques.
